description: Workbench-reviewed rhetoric and intent-pressure seed batch. Targets obfuscation, emotionally loaded framing, reckless accusation, argument from ignorance, and ulterior motive attribution while preserving belief movement at none.

entries.text: The spokesperson obfuscated the issue by using vague language.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The spokesperson obfuscated the issue by using vague language.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence marks clarity reduction or vague wording that makes the exact claim harder to inspect.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Obfuscation pressure is legitimate when wording, structure, or vagueness makes the exact claim harder to define, inspect, or test.

evidence_burden: Identify the exact claim being obscured.
Strip vague padding and restate the simplest inspectable claim.
Define ambiguous terms and check whether the obscurity changes the evidence burden.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: strip vague language and restate the simplest inspectable claim
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: request clearer evidence access and a simpler inspectable claim
questions: What exact claim is being obscured, and how can it be restated in the simplest testable form?

entries.text: He claims the policy failed because nobody has proven that it worked.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: He claims the policy failed because nobody has proven that it worked.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence moves from absence of proof or disproof into a truth or falsity conclusion.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A deictic reference is legitimate only when the referenced evidence, event, or claim is identified.
A policy-effectiveness claim is legitimate only with a defined outcome, baseline, timeframe, and comparison class.
Argument-from-ignorance pressure is legitimate when absence of proof is treated as proof of the opposite or absence of disproof is treated as proof of truth.

evidence_burden: Identify the referenced object.

Identify outcome metrics.
Compare against baseline and alternatives.

Identify whether the argument moves from absence of proof to falsity or absence of disproof to truth.
Check what evidence should exist if the claim were true or false.
Separate unresolved status from support or falsity.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: block absence-to-truth or absence-to-falsity movement and preserve unresolved status
